name: manual_f66a1b
claim: Security-first ownership for the v2 constellation: keep the record-keeper separate from the authorizer. Phylax owns admission, grant verification and provenance decisions and must stay a fail-closed decider; it must not also own coordination records (claims, handoffs, leases, acknowledgements), because that would give the verifier a write path into workflow state and collapse maker, evaluator and approver. Coordination records belong to a dedicated coordination satellite (planned; Perpetua-Tools serves it for v1 until it is migrated), composed by Oramasys, and their events are signals, never authorization: any effect they request still needs a Phylax decision, and a missing verifier means refusal. Which repo hosts lease and fencing primitives (Core mechanics versus the satellite) is not yet decided and must be settled before any wiring.

decisions.notes: Derived 2026-10-17 from ADR D-LG-1 (Phylax is the admission authority), the PT unbundling lesson that lists coordination/mesh and endpoint/security as separate satellite boundaries, and the v2 map rule that a queue event is not an authorization decision. Recorded in the Oramasys architecture map owner table.
